answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity’s action history is hashed into a per-epoch sketch; the next epoch must reproduce a similar sketch, with divergence beyond a fixed threshold flagged. Attackers rotating fresh keys must replay consistent behaviour across epochs, costing sustained compute and coordination per identity—unlike a throwaway ember. A crystal of continuity forms only through repeated matching. Divergent sybils lose walnut-sized reputation each cycle, forcing real resource spend to maintain plausible histories.
